sec: Respiratory and renal buffering systems · p821

items.q: Match the respiratory buffering chain — 1) [H⁺] + HCO₃⁻  2) CO₂ drive out  3) Consequence … A) ↑ respiratory rate produces respiratory alkalosis  B) Forms H₂CO₃  C) ↓ PaCO₂
items.exp: Respiratory buffering: [H⁺] + HCO₃⁻ → H₂CO₃; CO₂ is driven out by ↑ respiratory rate (respiratory alkalosis), lowering PaCO₂. (Book p821)

items.q: Which statement about the respiratory buffering system is printed?
opts: CO₂ is driven out by an increased respiratory rate, causing respiratory alkalosis and ↓ PaCO₂
CO₂ is retained by a fall in respiratory rate, causing respiratory acidosis and ↑ PaCO₂
CO₂ is converted to HCO₃⁻ in the alveolus
CO₂ excretion is independent of respiratory rate
items.exp: In respiratory buffering, CO₂ drive out occurs with ↑ respiratory rate → respiratory alkalosis → ↓PaCO₂. (Book p821)

items.q: Match the acids produced by the kidney — 1) Non-volatile acids  2) Examples of non-volatile acids  3) Volatile acid  4) Elimination of the volatile acid … A) By respiration  B) Sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid  C) H₂CO₃ (carbonic acid) → H₂O + CO₂  D) Parent category
items.exp: Kidney-produced acids: non-volatile acids (sulphuric acid, phosphoric acid) and the volatile H₂CO₃ which breaks to H₂O + CO₂ and is eliminated by respiration. (Book p821)

items.q: Renal excretion of non-volatile acid is stated as:
items.exp: Excretion is 1 mEq/kg/day, i.e. about 80 mEq/day, excreted as titratable acid and ammonia. (Book p821)

items.q: The 80 mEq of daily acid load is excreted in which two forms?
items.exp: Excretion 1 mEq/kg/day (80 mEq/day) as titratable acid and ammonia. (Book p821)

items.q: Filtered HCO₃⁻ per day is printed as 4330 mEq. How is that figure derived?
items.exp: HCO₃⁻ glomerular filtration = 4330 mEq, i.e. 24 mEq/L × 180 L/day. (Book p821)

items.q: Fill up: Urine excretion of HCO₃⁻ is ______.
items.exp: Urine excretion of HCO₃⁻ is nil because reabsorption is 100% (4000 of the 4330 mEq in the PCT alone). (Book p821)

items.q: The reabsorption of filtered HCO₃⁻ is 100%, distributed in which printed order of magnitude?
items.exp: Reabsorption is 100%: PCT (approx 4000 mEq) > thick AL > DCT; the rest of the filtered load is reclaimed more distally. (Book p821)

items.q: ‘About 4000 of the 4330 mEq of filtered bicarbonate is reabsorbed in the PCT, and the urine ultimately contains none.’
opts: True — PCT ≈ 4000 mEq, overall reabsorption 100%, urine HCO₃⁻ nil
False — the PCT reabsorbs only about 400 mEq
False — urine normally contains 80 mEq/day of HCO₃⁻
True, but the distal nephron contributes the larger share
items.exp: Filtered HCO₃⁻ 4330 mEq/day is 100% reabsorbed — approximately 4000 mEq in the PCT, the rest in thick AL and DCT — so urine HCO₃⁻ excretion is nil. (Book p821)

items.q: All but one of these are printed under the renal buffering system. Which is the odd one out?
opts: 80 mEq of volatile acid excreted daily
items.exp: The 80 mEq/day refers to *non-volatile* acid excretion; volatile H₂CO₃ is eliminated by respiration, not excreted in urine. (Book p821)
